title: A second person inside each customer
where: At the till and the repair bar, every customer, first person
wrong: A blonde woman in a red coat is drawn inside every customer you serve. Her hair and red sleeve stick out, and one guest showed two faces.
fix: In Unity, play a day, select a served customer and switch off the extra body drawn inside them.
caption: Blonde hair and a red coat stick out behind Valerie; Beatriz has a second face under hers.

title: The cloth in Ace's hand
where: The bench close-up, centre screen, whenever Ace wipes a phone
wrong: The cloth is a smooth yellow cone that looks like a rubber duck. The folded cloth in its tray, and the Wipe icon, look right.
fix: In Unity, hold the folded tray cloth flat on the screen and wipe in circles; R3 would rather have a new Blender cloth over a fingertip.
caption: The yellow cone on the phone is the cloth; second picture: it beside the folded cloth.

title: The support-call phone is a grey block
where: From Day 4: at the counter, in the tray, in Ace's hand
wrong: The phone for support calls is a plain grey box. The detailed phone model already in the game isn't used for it.
fix: In Unity, give the support-call phone the detailed phone's parts, then rerun Bench 7's layout and check it fits the intake tray.
caption: The support-call phone today is a grey slab; second picture: the detailed phone it should use.

title: Seated customers lose their heads
where: Seated guests seen from about 2 m, walking in first person
wrong: From some angles a seated customer's head, hair and hat vanish while the body still shows. You see through the open collar.
fix: In Unity, tick 'Update When Offscreen' on each customer's head, hair and hat, then check again with the NpcSit lab.
caption: From the side the hard-hat man has no head; from the front he has it.

title: The black lid behind the bins man
where: At the bins, every talk with the man, Nights 0 and 2
wrong: When his dumpster lid is open, its underside is a flat pure-black slab right behind his head. In the story's key scene it looks like a hole.
fix: In Unity, paint the lid's underside the same green as its top in the Night 0 step, or open it less (about 75°) so it doesn't face the camera.
caption: The black slab behind his head is the open lid's underside; second picture: the lid lifting.

title: West Street's two ball trees
where: West Street, by the brick corner shop: night and morning intro
wrong: Each tree is three smooth green balls on an orange pipe. Next to the street's other trees they look like stand-ins.
fix: In Unity, switch off the two ball trees and put Kenney oak or small trees in their place, as was done for the courtyard.
caption: Smooth green balls on an orange pipe, beside the street's real trees.

title: The patio's flower in a vase
where: The patio table; a close-up in the Day 4 and 5 intros
wrong: The flower is a yellow ball on a red tube. Filmed up close in the intro, it reads as a chess pawn, not a flower.
fix: In Unity, swap the ball and tube for the Kenney yellow flower in a small pot, or cut the flower shot from the intro.
caption: A yellow ball on a red tube stands in for the flower.

title: The coffee in the cup
where: In Ace's hand at the drinks machine, every drink
wrong: A finished coffee is a flat near-white disc, like milk; another came out grey-beige, like dishwater. Neither looks like coffee.
fix: In Unity, colour coffee, espresso and americano a dark roast brown with a lighter ring (latte tan, cocoa brown, tea amber), and find why two coffees differ.
caption: Two finished coffees: one milk-white, one grey-beige.

title: The black cup and lid station
where: The back bar beside the drinks machine, at eye level, every drink
wrong: From where Ace stands, the cup station is three all-black tubes on a black board. It's the darkest thing on the cream tiles.
fix: In Unity, make the tubes brushed steel with the green sticker band, and the board walnut.
caption: From Ace's spot it reads as black boards; head-on (second picture) you see the cups.

title: The drinks machine's button words
where: Head-on at the drinks machine, every drink
wrong: Each word is sized to fit its own button, so TEA and LATTE are huge and AMERICANO is tiny. Six sizes in one row look unfinished.
fix: In Unity, turn off auto-size on the six labels and give them all the size AMERICANO needs, with HOT CHOCOLATE on two lines.
caption: TEA and LATTE stand about 2.5 times taller than AMERICANO.

title: The milky glass on the bench screen
where: First person at the bench; also the water station and grinder
wrong: The clear screen lays a pale haze over the room behind it. The same glass makes the water glasses solid white and the grinder look full of flour.
fix: In Unity, make the café glass much less shiny (smoothness about 0.5) in the kit's own settings so a re-run keeps it, and make the water more see-through.
caption: Below the screen's top edge the room turns pale; second picture: the glasses and hopper read white.

title: The phone's insides
where: The bench close-up, once the phone's back cover is off
wrong: Inside are flat cut-outs on a brown plate: no circuit board, chips, screws or cables. Next to the detailed back cover it looks like a stand-in.
fix: In Blender, add a green circuit board with a few chips, a labelled battery, two ribbon cables and a copper charging coil, in the same footprint.
caption: A cream bar, a peach ring and two discs stand in for the phone's insides.

title: The photo-plaster boards by the windows
where: The café's east wall behind the notice board, seen from the bench
wrong: Tall beige boards with a grainy photo pattern stand in front of the windows, like boards leaning on the glass. Nothing else in the room has a photo pattern.
fix: In Unity, give that one wall part the back wall's flat 'Oat plaster' and leave the street's copies alone; a Blender pillar that meets the window frames can come later.
caption: Grainy beige boards stand in front of the glass, the notice board on one.

title: The patio A-frame only half stands
where: The pavement right of the café door, from above and the street
wrong: Only the chalkboard side stands up. The plain back leans behind it with its foot off the ground, and the two never meet at the top.
fix: In Blender, rebuild it as a true A: both sides leaning from one hinge, both feet down, a chalk face on each side.
caption: From the side the two boards don't meet; from the street the back one leans loose.

title: Twin walkers in red coats
where: West Street's pavement in the morning intro, from its first frame
wrong: Two identical blonde women in the same red coat walk in step. It looks like a copy bug.
fix: In Unity, give the walkers different Synty looks and start them at different points on their route.
caption: Two identical women in red coats, in step.

title: The bare uphill road at the edge
where: The intro's first street shot, pull-outs and titles; West Street at night
wrong: The streets go on as long empty ramps into haze, with nothing either side. It sits where the eye goes in the game's first shot.
fix: In Unity, aim the intro's street shot and pull-outs so the ramp leaves the frame, or line its first 30 m with the hill's Synty buildings.
caption: The road runs on as an empty ramp into haze; second picture: the same in the Day 1 title.

title: Grace's yellow house looks brown
where: 12 West Street, at night and in the Day 2 intro
wrong: The night's directions say 'the yellow house', but it reads dark brown at night and dull ochre by day. Only the curtains are yellow.
fix: In Unity, give her house its own clear warm yellow paint (about #E9B43C), keep the plaster only for its bumps, and check it under the porch light.
caption: Her house reads brown at night; by day (second picture) it's dull ochre with yellow curtains.

title: Grace's porch lamp is a bare ball
where: Her front door, from her step and across the street
wrong: Her porch light is a glowing ball with no lamp around it. Up close it looks like a small ghost.
fix: In Unity, put the glow inside a small lantern, like the lamp by the bins, and shrink the ball to bulb size.
caption: The glowing ball over her door has no lamp around it.

title: Blank orange walls in the pull-outs
where: The tilted pull-outs and titles of the Day 3 to 6 intros
wrong: The biggest things on screen are two flat orange building sides with no windows. In normal play they barely show.
fix: In Unity, re-aim those pull-outs, or turn the two blocks so a side with windows shows.
caption: Two windowless orange slabs fill the Day 3 pull-out.

title: The coat and scarf on Grace's stand
where: Grace's front room, the corner by the TV, on night break-ins
wrong: The coat is one long capsule with no shoulders, collar or sleeves, and the scarf is two stiff red bars. It's the café coats' 'squares and rectangles' again.
fix: In Blender, delete the coat and the two scarf bars, keep the hat and stand, and re-export (about 5 minutes).
caption: A capsule coat and two red bars for a scarf; the hat and stand are fine.

title: Grace's floor lamp shade from below
where: Her front room by her armchair, crouched in first person
wrong: The shade is drawn on one side only, so from below its inside is missing and the lit shade vanishes. From above it looks fine.
fix: In Unity, set the lampshade material to draw both sides; that also fixes her bedside lamp and the house kit pendant.
caption: From below, the red part is the shade's inside, which isn't drawn; from above it looks fine.

title: Grace asleep has no head
where: Her bedroom, when the player sneaks upstairs past her bed
wrong: Asleep, Grace is only this quilt: a stiff tray with a long mound and nothing on the pillow. It reads as an empty bed with a bump.
fix: In Blender, add the back of a head in her hair colour on the left pillow, soften the quilt's sides, and re-export.
caption: The quilt's mound runs up to an empty pillow.

title: The brush's bristles
where: On the tool rest, in every bench close-up
wrong: The bristles are 6 to 8 separate orange rods splayed like a fork. It reads more like a rake than a brush.
fix: In Blender, make the bristles one tapered block with a few grooves; R1 counted the brush among the good tools.
caption: Separate orange rods fan out like a rake.

title: Lamp shadows like stains on the bench
where: The bench close-up, on the wood and the mat
wrong: The magnifier lamp throws a soft dark ring on the wood and a dark band across the mat. They read as stains.
fix: In Unity, stop the magnifier lamp casting shadows into the close-up.
caption: The dark ring on the wood (top left) is a shadow; the band on the mat (second picture) is faint.

title: The help outline breaks into dashes
where: The bench close-up, on the opened phone
wrong: The amber help line breaks into dashes along the frame's edge and floats in pieces over the middle. Two surfaces fight at the same depth.
fix: In Unity, push the outline a little further out, or draw it on top of everything.
caption: Ringed: the help line breaks into dashes down the right edge and floats in the middle.

title: The leftover smudge on the dirty phone
where: The bench close-up, after wiping the gunked phone
wrong: One leftover smudge is a flat white cloud with a fuzzy edge. It looks like a sticker, while the rest of the dirt looks real.
fix: In Unity, make that smudge a see-through grey-brown.
caption: The white cloud on the screen is the leftover smudge.

title: The watch's small seconds hand
where: The bench close-up and the counter, whenever the pocket watch comes
wrong: The small seconds hand turns over bare dial, with no little ring or ticks under it. Up close it reads as a stray scratch.
fix: In the dial texture, add a small ring with 12 ticks under that hand.
caption: Just left of the 6, the tiny hand sits on bare dial.

title: The grey sheet on Grace's camera
where: The bench close-up, over the camera's gear block
wrong: A grey sheet over the gear block reads as crumpled paper. It's not clear what it is on an otherwise excellent camera.
fix: Keep it, unless it's meant to be something; check the model in Blender.
caption: The crumpled grey sheet sits over the brass gears.

title: The bare ruler on Ace's desk mat
where: First person at the bench, lower left of the screen
wrong: The steel ruler is a bare light-grey bar with no marks. It reads as a stray strip.
fix: In Unity, give the ruler a texture with marks and numbers.
caption: Ringed: the plain grey bar on the dark mat is meant to be a steel ruler.

title: The loud colours on Ace's desk
where: First person at the bench, beside the blue repair mat
wrong: The wire spools are pure red and green, the mug bright green and the meter pure yellow. They're the loudest colours in the café.
fix: In Unity, tone the spools, mug and meter toward the kit's sage, brick and mustard.
caption: Pure red and green spools, a bright green mug and a yellow meter.

title: The magnifier lamp's flat springs
where: First person at the bench, right edge of the screen
wrong: The lamp's springs are flat black wavy ribbons lying on the arm and the post. They read as scribbles or tape, not coils.
fix: In Blender, make them round coil tubes, or delete the two springs.
caption: Ringed: the flat black wavy strips on the arm and post are the springs.

title: White squares under the bench top
where: Under the bench top's front edge, whenever Ace stands there
wrong: A black bar of grey and white squares, one pure white, runs under the bench top. It reads as a stray strip or blank labels.
fix: In Unity, select it in the Scene view and fix or switch it off; R4 thinks it's a power strip that can stay.
caption: The black bar of white squares under the bench edge; R4 reads it as a power strip.

title: The donor parts box under the bench
where: Under the bench, looking down or walking past
wrong: A plain red box on a plain blue box sits beside a grey box with a scribbled card. The old phones, remote, router and cable it should hold don't come across.
fix: In Unity, switch it off; a Blender tangle of cable and two face-down phones only if you want it back.
caption: Plain red, blue and grey boxes stand in for a box of old parts.

title: The till's blank keys and screen
where: First person at the till, and in the talk camera
wrong: The keys are blank white and the screen is an empty green panel, on an otherwise good till.
fix: In Unity, add a texture with the key labels, and a price on the screen.
caption: Blank white keys and an empty green screen.

title: The blocky bulb in the counter lamp
where: First person at the till, top left of the screen
wrong: Inside the smooth lamp shade hangs a blocky egg for a bulb.
fix: In Unity, swap in a smooth sphere for the bulb, or smooth it in Blender.
caption: Ringed: the bulb is a blocky egg inside a smooth shade.

title: Ace's head fills the talk camera
where: Talking to Grace at the counter, left side of the screen
wrong: Ace's blocky hair and flat ear fill the left fifth of the screen. Nothing else that close is so coarse.
fix: In Unity, move the conversation camera about 20 cm further from his shoulder.
caption: Ringed: Ace's blocky hair and ear fill the left of the shot.

title: The condiment tray's plain blocks
where: The counter's lowered end, on the customer side
wrong: The tray holds a cup of stirrers, then a white block, a black box, a brown brick and a black pot. The blocks read as blocks.
fix: In Blender, make sugar packets in a caddy, a stack of lids and a labelled shaker.
caption: Plain blocks on the tray stand in for sugar, lids and shakers.

title: Two stray rods by the cup stack
where: First person at the drinks machine, beside the cup stack
wrong: Two thin dark rods stand loose at the corners of the cup base, touching nothing. They read as stray sticks.
fix: In Unity, switch off the two 'Cup caddy rail' parts in the machine's prefab; or, in Blender, join their tops with a ring.
caption: Ringed: the two loose rods beside the paper cups.

title: The drinks machine's blank top panel
where: Head-on at the drinks machine
wrong: The cream band across the top is plain. It's the biggest blank surface on the main machine.
fix: In Unity, add a small enamel ACE'S badge in the middle.
caption: Ringed: the plain cream band over the buttons.

title: Noisy labels on the syrup bottles
where: The syrup rack, left of the drinks machine
wrong: The white label bands carry a grey cloudy noise. Nothing else on the flat bottles is noisy.
fix: In Unity, give the labels a flat colour.
caption: Grey cloudy noise on the bottles' white labels.

title: The wrapped repairs on the pickup row
where: The back bar under the parts drawers, behind the counter
wrong: The lamp wrapped in paper looks like a giant crayon or a baguette. The paper bags are crisp boxes with one flat flap.
fix: In Blender, twist the lamp's paper shut with its shade and base showing, and crumple the bag tops; R2 would wait for the next Blender pass, and R3 thinks the bags read fine.
caption: Right ring: the paper-wrapped lamp; left ring: the two paper bags.

title: The game controller in its bag
where: The pickup row on the back bar, in the background
wrong: The game controller in its zip bag is so small it looks like a tiny dark gun on a card.
fix: In Blender, make the controller bigger in its bag.
caption: Ringed: the small dark controller on its card.

title: Customers' knees inside the repair bar
where: Guests on the repair-bar stools, seen from the bench or floor
wrong: Seated guests' knees and shins go inside the bar's front panel. The stools sit too close to the bar for the pose.
fix: In Unity, move the stools and their sit points about 10 cm back.
caption: Ringed: her knee and shin pass into the bar's front.

title: Plain grey box seen from the stools
where: From a repair-bar stool, looking across at Ace's desk
wrong: A plain grey box sits at a seated guest's eye level. It's the blank back of Ace's small-parts drawers.
fix: In Blender, give the drawers a back panel with a rim and a label, so they read as a cabinet from the stools.
caption: The grey box beside the spools is the drawers' blank back; second picture: the desk from behind.

title: Jagged window shadows on the floor
where: Every daytime overhead, and at floor level by the windows
wrong: The window shadows have stair-step edges. It looks like a rendering fault.
fix: In Unity's URP settings, turn on soft shadows, or raise the sun's shadow resolution, or shorten the shadow distance.
caption: The window frames' shadows have stair-step edges.

title: Many guests in one red jacket
where: The café from above in busy hours
wrong: About half the guests wear the same red jacket with a green or red cap or hair, as if one outfit were copied.
fix: In Unity, add more colour versions for each guest who arrives.
caption: Red jackets and caps repeat across the room.

title: Every customer looks cross
where: Close up in talks, at the counter and at tables
wrong: Every face has heavy black brows angled down and a flat mouth, so up close all the guests look cross. That works against 'chaos with a hint of cozy'.
fix: In Unity, make a softer brow and eye version of the shared face texture.
caption: Heavy angled brows and a flat mouth on two different guests.

title: The plain napkin boxes on tables
where: On every table, in first person and in talks
wrong: Each napkin holder is a plain light-grey cube with a white slot, bigger than the cups. From the counter they read as white cups.
fix: In Blender, round the edges, give it a chrome or wood body and make it about 20% smaller (or, in Unity, just a chrome material).
caption: A plain grey cube, bigger than the paper cups beside it.

title: The stiff tote bags on the floor
where: At the stools' feet by the long table
wrong: The tote is a stiff blocky bag; side-on it's a pale egg-shaped rock with two sticks. Once the coats go, it's the last soft thing built as a solid.
fix: In Blender, make a slumped canvas bag with an opening and a fold; R2 judged the model soft enough already.
caption: A stiff bag on the floor; second picture: the model from the front and the side.

title: The laptop screens look dead
where: The laptop workers at the long table
wrong: The open laptop's screen is a flat light-blue panel. It reads as a dead screen.
fix: In Unity, put a two-tone screen texture on it: a dark title bar over a page.
caption: Ringed: the flat blue screen.

title: The pale lounge rug
where: The window lounge, from the overhead camera
wrong: From above, the rug reads as a pale sheet of paper on the grey floor, barely wider than the table. Its stripes hide under the chairs.
fix: In Unity, tint the rug deeper (rust or teal, or toward #C49A6C) and/or scale it up so the chairs' front feet stand on it.
caption: Ringed: the pale rug under the low table; second picture: the rug itself.

title: The glowing window ledge
where: Along the bottom of the east windows, in first person
wrong: The ledge is a long pale-yellow plank, brighter than anything else in shadow. It looks unlit or glowing.
fix: In Unity, give the café side the counter's oak or the sage joinery colour.
caption: Ringed: the pale yellow plank along the windows.

title: The spiky olive trees by the door
where: Inside the door: the first thing a walking player passes
wrong: The tree tops are blocky balls bristling with leaf shards like spikes. At eye level they read as a cactus or thorny pods, not soft olive leaves.
fix: In Blender, delete the spiky leaf cards so the soft balls read as a trimmed tree; or, in Unity, put a second fig there instead.
caption: Blocky balls with spiky leaf cards, at eye level.

title: Black mats on the staff floor
where: Behind the counter, from the overhead camera
wrong: From above, the rubber mats are plain black shapes that read as holes in the floor. At eye level they read as mats.
fix: In Unity, give them the till mat's rubber texture, or a dark brown rubber.
caption: Ringed: a plain black shape on the staff floor.

title: A shading seam on the back door
where: First person at the back door, every night
wrong: The frame's inner face shows a lighter triangle, a shading seam where it should look flat.
fix: In Blender, mark the frame's edges sharp, or set its smoothing angle to 0 in Unity's import settings.
caption: Ringed: the lighter wedge on the door frame's inner face.

title: The banquette's missing back
where: The west-wall banquette, from the sidewalk through the glass
wrong: The padded backrest has no back, so from behind only the top rail floats over the seat. It matters more if it ever becomes furniture you can place.
fix: In Blender, close the back with one plain panel, or in Unity put a thin dark box behind it.
caption: From behind only the rails show; red on the right is the back the game doesn't draw.

title: The child's drawing on the notice board
where: The café's notice board
wrong: The model check flagged it as see-through, but that's only its back, which lies against the cork. On the board it reads fine.
fix: Nothing to do: it's a false alarm.
caption: On the board the drawing reads well; the flag picture shows only its back.

title: The patio table's glowing white top
where: The table outside the café door, in every overhead
wrong: Its 'marble' is one flat near-white with no veins, so it glows like a white blob. It's still the brightest thing outside at 8 pm.
fix: In Unity, tint it to the counter's warm grey or use the café's own round table; give all Tier 2 tables a veined marble before the shop sells them.
caption: A white blob with a halo by day; still glowing at 8 pm.

title: Boulder plants in the door planters
where: Either side of the café door, from above and the pavement
wrong: Each trough holds three big blocky green boulders, a metre from the café's own leafy plants. From above they read as gems or cabbages.
fix: In Unity, put the café's rubber plant, or the Kenney bushes already on the street, in the troughs.
caption: Blocky green boulders in the trough; second picture: both troughs from above.

title: The Tier 2 brass looks like paint
where: The patio table's base; all Tier 2 shop pieces later
wrong: The Tier 2 brass has no shine, so it reads as mustard paint, as the furniture catalogue warned.
fix: In Unity, make the brass a little paler and softer in colour.
caption: The mustard-yellow base under the patio table's white top.

title: The chunky patio chairs
where: The patio table outside the door; the intro's flower close-up
wrong: The Kenney chairs are heavy and toy-like next to the café's slim chairs inside. From above they're fine.
fix: In Unity, swap them for the café's own chairs; R4 would keep them unless the intro keeps its patio close-up.
caption: Ringed: the chunky arched-back chair at eye level.

title: The A-frame's dim chalk
where: The A-frame on the pavement, seen from the street
wrong: The chalk is dim grey on charcoal (about 1.9 to 1), so the good words fade from across the street. Up close by day you can read it.
fix: Repaint the chalk near-white (#E8E4DA) with one amber or green line; R3 counted the A-frame sign as good, so look first.
caption: The chalk words are grey, not white; readable up close, dim from farther away.

title: West Street's cube lanterns
where: West Street in first person, and the intro's café-sign shot
wrong: Each lamp is a plain glowing or cream cube on a pole. Fine from above, a plain box up close.
fix: Keep, or swap them for the Synty lamp posts the other streets use.
caption: A plain glowing cube on a pole at night; a cream cube by day.

title: The bins man's face in close-up
where: The bins talk camera; also two walkers in the intro
wrong: His flat pale face has a black bar across the eyes, like a censor bar. It may be meant, for a man who hides.
fix: Keep (they're Synty sunglasses); if it bothers you, swap in a hat or other glasses.
caption: A black bar across his eyes; an intro walker has the same.

title: The car park's ball bushes
where: Across the front street from the café, only ever small
wrong: The planted island is five smooth sage balls round a tree, the same ball plants as the sidewalk trees.
fix: In Unity, once the sidewalk trees are done, swap the balls for the Kenney bushes the planted pockets use.
caption: Ringed: smooth sage balls at the tree's foot.

title: The window-box shrubs at night
where: The café door, in first person at night
wrong: At night the window-box shrubs read as crumpled dark paper. By day they're fine.
fix: Nothing to do.
caption: Dark crumpled shapes in the window box at night.

title: The white tiled tower behind the sign
where: The intro's shot of the café front
wrong: A plain white grid tower above ACE'S CAFÉ reads like bathroom tiles.
fix: Keep (it's a background Synty office); tilt the shot if it bothers you.
caption: The plain white grid box above the café's name.

title: Barcode lit windows at night
where: The big brick block west of Grace's, from above at night
wrong: Lit windows show as bars in threes and fours, like a barcode.
fix: Keep: they're Synty's lit blinds, as made.
caption: Lit blinds drawn as bars in threes and fours.

title: A traffic light over Grace's door
where: The Day 2 intro's shot of Grace's house
wrong: A traffic signal post stands across her door and window, in the middle of the shot.
fix: In Unity, move that shot's camera about 1 m along the pavement.
caption: Ringed: the signal post across her door.

title: The cardboard-looking panel on Grace's door
where: Her door in first person and in her intro shot
wrong: A flat tan rectangle on her dark green door looks like cardboard taped on.
fix: In Unity, paint the door panel in the door's own dark colour, a shade lighter, so it reads as a sunk panel.
caption: Ringed: the flat tan panel on the green door.

title: The blank side wall of Grace's house
where: Coming up the cross street in first person
wrong: The house's open side is a flat brown slab; the timber strips run along the front only.
fix: In Unity, run the same timber strips down the house's side (low priority).
caption: Ringed: the flat brown side of her corner house.

title: Grace's empty photo frames
where: Grace's front room, stairs and bedroom, on night break-ins
wrong: Every photo is the same flat sepia colour, so every frame looks empty. Her story is a reunion, yet there are no faces on her walls.
fix: In Unity, put one small painted snapshot (a sky and two or three people) on the photo material; a picture per frame can come later as 2D art.
caption: The photos in two of her frames are flat blank colour.

title: The reunion cups look like a tube
where: Grace's worktop on Night 2, then Ace's trophy shelf
wrong: The sleeve of twelve paper cups reads as a smooth rolled tube or a scroll. The cup rims barely show.
fix: In Blender, give the sleeve 13 rings and a 0.85 narrow radius (not 7 and 0.94) and re-export; the cup box's sleeves improve too.
caption: A smooth tube where stacked cup rims should show.

title: Grace's doors look like flat slabs
where: The doors inside Grace's house, on night break-ins
wrong: Face-on, the four panels vanish and each door reads as a flat slab with a knob. The panels show only as hairlines at an angle.
fix: In Blender, sink the panels about 8 mm, or add a darker inner line.
caption: Face-on (left) the door is a blank slab; at an angle the panels show as hairlines.

title: A black block at Grace's stairs
where: Inside Grace's house at night, front left of the stairs
wrong: A black block sits at the foot of her stairs. The dark upstairs is meant; this may be the unlit cupboard under the stairs.
fix: Keep for now, but check what the black block is.
caption: Ringed: the black block at the foot of her stairs.

title: The black frame round the phone's cover
where: The bench close-up with the phone, and the intro's bench shot
wrong: Four dark steel walls of the old parts tray were left on with no floor. They make a thick black frame that runs off the mat and over the new screen's pad.
fix: Builder C is switching off the whole old tray this session (Bench 7b and Bench 7).
caption: The thick black frame on the right is the old tray's walls.

title: The mat's ruler cut in half
where: The bench close-up with the phone, bottom of the screen
wrong: The bottom of the screen cuts the mat's ruler numbers in half, so the strip reads like a mistake.
fix: Builder C's new Bench 9 framing rule fixes it this session: the ruler shows whole, or just its numbers with the ticks running off.
caption: Ringed: the ruler's numbers cut in half by the screen's bottom edge.

title: The coats on the banquette chairs
where: Two chairs on the café's west wall, overhead and in first person
wrong: Each coat is one flat slab bent over the chair, with stiff tube sleeves and no folds, in a cold grey. They're your 'squares and rectangles'.
fix: Builder C is switching both off this session (Art tidy 1) and stops Lived in 2 putting them back; a draped Blender coat only if you want coats back.
caption: The coats from behind; second picture: the two dark slabs on the chairs from above.

title: The coat stand's box scarf and tote
where: The café's waiting nook; switched off since 9 Oct
wrong: The scarf and Ace's tote on the café's coat stand are plain boxes. The stand has been off since 9 Oct, so players don't see them now.
fix: Builder C is switching the scarf and tote off this session and keeping the stand and its hat.
caption: No photo shows it (off since 9 Oct); this is the waiting nook today.

title: Tier 1 shop furniture comes in flat
where: Not seen today; once you buy and place furniture
wrong: The shop's Tier 1 chairs, bench and tub chair carry flat wood colour, while the café's own furniture has grain. A piece placed while playing would come in flat.
fix: In Unity, give these models the café's grain materials as the café kit does, or have the furniture shop apply the same swap when it places a piece.
caption: Left: the shop's chair in flat colour; right: the café's own chair with wood grain.

title: House kit pendant: see-through from below
where: Not placed yet; meant for a house ceiling, seen from below
wrong: The shade is drawn on one side only, so from below you see the bulb and ceiling through it. Hung as it is, it would look broken.
fix: In Unity, set the lampshade material to draw both sides; the same change fixes Grace's floor lamp.
caption: From below, red shows the shade's inside, which isn't drawn.

title: House kit pendant: a closed top
where: Not placed yet; meant for a house ceiling
wrong: The shade's top is closed, so it reads as a hat rather than a drum shade.
fix: In Blender, give the shade a real wall thickness and an open top.
caption: The pendant from above and the side: a closed cap, like a hat.

title: House kit paintings show the wrong part
where: Not placed yet; meant for Grace's walls at night
wrong: Each canvas shows the wrong slice of its picture: a sail cut off, a hard seam, a portrait with no head.
fix: In Unity, set each painting material's tiling and offset to R2's numbers (check one first), or unwrap each canvas to fit in Blender.
caption: Harbour, Portrait, Hills and Still: a cut sail, a blank field, a seam, a blob.

title: House kit door: glass buried inside
where: Not placed yet; meant as a street door, seen at night
wrong: The glass sits inside the solid door, so the window reads as four painted panels and a cross pokes out the back. The back has no panels or knob.
fix: In Blender, cut the window opening out of the door so a lit hall shows through; back panels and a knob only if a hall is seen.
caption: The window reads as painted panels; the back (right) is a bare board.

title: House kit mug has no floor
where: Not placed yet; meant for a table or a counter
wrong: The mug's inside floor is missing, so from above you look straight through it.
fix: In Blender, close the mug's inside floor (one setting, cap_top=True, on that spin).
caption: From above, the mug's inside is a hole (red: not drawn).

title: House kit coat on the hook
where: Not placed yet; meant for Grace's hall, seen up close
wrong: The coat is a tapered column with two tube sleeves beside it and no shoulders, lapels or folds. The red scarf is buried in its front.
fix: In Blender, make a coat hanging from its loop with folds, sleeves joined at the shoulder and the scarf over the hook; or never place it.
caption: A column with tube sleeves; from the side, a plank.

title: House kit shoes and slippers
where: Not placed yet; meant for Grace's hall floor
wrong: Each shoe is a blocky lump on a flat board bigger than it, with no opening or toe shape. The slippers are pink soap bars on the same boards.
fix: In Blender, make a sole with a shoe's outline and an upper that hugs it with an opening, before placing them.
caption: Shoes like loaves on boards; slippers like pink soap bars.

title: House kit cushion is a slab
where: Not placed yet; meant for a sofa or an armchair
wrong: The cushion is a bevelled mustard slab with a flat top and straight sides, like a block of butter.
fix: In Blender, dome both big faces 30 to 40 mm and pinch the corners.
caption: A flat mustard slab with straight sides.

title: House kit open book is blank
where: Not placed yet; meant for a table
wrong: The pages are two flat blank slabs with a gap at the spine. Half the cover's underside is also inside out, seen only from below.
fix: In Blender, curve the pages up from the spine, add a few grey text bars and flip that half of the cover.
caption: Two flat cream slabs with a gap at the spine.

title: House kit radiator is a blank board
where: Not placed yet; meant for a wall at eye height
wrong: Its fins sit between two flat panels, so from the front and back it's a blank cream board on two feet.
fix: In Blender, cut 12 to 14 upright grooves in the front panel, or make it a column radiator.
caption: A blank board from the front; the fins show only from below.

title: House kit newspaper looks like a grid
where: Not placed yet; meant for a table
wrong: The print is three solid ink slabs cut by a raised fold, so from above it's a dark six-pane grid, more tray than paper.
fix: In Blender, make each column 6 to 8 thin ink lines and one grey photo block, with a crease for the fold, or use a printed texture.
caption: Solid dark blocks read as a grid, not print.

title: House kit round rug is a target
where: Not placed yet; meant for a floor, seen from above
wrong: A cream border, a teal field, a thin cream ring and a rust dot make an archery target.
fix: In Blender, swap the dot and inner ring for a medallion or a star, or use a texture.
caption: Rings and a centre dot, like an archery target.

title: The old counter and espresso machine
where: Not seen: both are switched off in the 20 Oct scene
wrong: Two boxy early pieces, a shiny plastic-looking counter and a flat-backed machine, are left in the scene switched off.
fix: In Unity, delete both from the scene so a later step can't switch them back on.
caption: The old counter's shiny plastic top and the old boxy machine.

title: The old 'Little plant'
where: Not seen: its window-lounge copy is switched off
wrong: Two blocky green balls on a pot, far below the café's own leafy plants: a gem among leaves.
fix: If a small plant is wanted there or in the shop, use the house kit plant or the café's pothos, and leave this one off.
caption: Left: the blocky 'Little plant'; right: the café's own pothos.

title: The old mug with a solid top
where: Not seen: its window-ledge copy is switched off
wrong: A solid cylinder with a handle: no opening, no rim and no coffee.
fix: In Unity, use the bar mat's mugs or the Synty mug on the counter instead.
caption: The top is a closed flat disc, with no opening.

title: The old grey drink cup
where: Not seen: every cup comes dressed from the machine's cup stack
wrong: A plain default-grey cylinder, thinner than the machine's paper cups. It stays hidden because every cup is dressed as a paper cup.
fix: Leave it hidden; any old cup path that comes back must dress its cup the same way.
caption: Left: the plain grey cup; right: the machine whose cup stack dresses every cup.

title: The patron's default beach body
where: Not seen: every seated patron is re-dressed on arrival
wrong: The default patron is a man in a tank top, board shorts and flip-flops: beachwear in a San Francisco café. It shows only if both re-dress systems fail.
fix: Nothing to do while the re-dress systems work.
caption: The default body: tank top, red board shorts, flip-flops.
